solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arguments in studios apt to get out of control

indicators.note: letters that get out of control run wild and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: Rows break out in studios when tempers are likely to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get out of control' rearranges the twelve letters of IN STUDIOS APT.
explanation.definitionFit: Disputations are formal debates or quarrels, so they are arguments in the plural.

clue.text: Trendy church's leader, silly rector is wrong

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so this takes the first letter of the word church's
silly suggests the letters are behaving foolishly and fall into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fashionable vicar's daft superior is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' is the anagram signal, not a description of the rector; 'leader' takes just the opening letter of church's.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrect and wrong are plain synonyms for something not true or not accurate.

clue.text: Broody writers this writer's taken after

indicators.note: taken after says the second piece is placed behind the first

parts.note: this writer is the setter, so 'this writer has' is I'VE

explanation.surface: Moody authors are followed by the setter himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer's' is the setter speaking of himself: I have, contracted to I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Broody can mean thoughtful and melancholy, a close synonym for lost in sombre thought.

clue.text: Top lady entertained by excellent boozers

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within, so the lady goes inside the other word

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the top lady in Britain

explanation.surface: A grand lady is hosted by splendid drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the late Queen's royal cipher, a crossword stock abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a heavy habitual drinker, so boozers in the plural.

clue.text: Street set up trial runs

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' says the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A road is prepared for practice laps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ST plus SET, giving TESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests are trials or experiments, much like practice runs before the real thing.

clue.text: Cells with circular shape, having very small area

parts.note: A, a small letter, abbreviates area

explanation.surface: Round cells occupy a tiny region.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova are egg cells, the female reproductive cells of animals.

clue.text: Where a rat's destroyed a bird

indicators.note: destroyed suggests the words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A rodent has ruined a bird's nest somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The shearwater is a seabird that skims low over the waves.

clue.text: Picture of prisoner brought to India

indicators.note: brought to says the first word is attached after the second

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An image of a convict taken to the subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a religious image, or more generally a small symbolic image.

clue.text: Fool nabbed by servant in corridor

indicators.note: something nabbed by another is seized and held inside it

parts.note: a page is a young servant

explanation.surface: An idiot is caught by a footman in the hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a narrow way between rooms, synonymous with a hallway.

clue.text: Perceive the true nature of what must be transparent?

definitions.meaning: to see past a front to the reality underneath
a sheer fabric or window you can look right past

explanation.surface: Understanding the reality of something that ought to be clear.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means penetrating a deception; the hyphenated adjective describes glass or fabric that is clear.

clue.text: Former member of the Lords? That is right

parts.note: an earl is a peer who may sit in the House of Lords
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: An ex-peer is confirmed as correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Former and earlier both describe something preceding in time.

clue.text: Part of flight from Budapest airport

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A leg of an air journey leaving Hungary's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made up of steps, each one a single step in the series.

clue.text: Asti on tap — novel provision for start of Italian meal

definitions.text: provision for start of Italian meal

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Italian sparkling wine served on draught, an unusual way to begin dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges ASTI ON TAP. Asti is an Italian sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian appetiser course of cured meats and vegetables served first.

clue.text: Those people, leaders of English Society, offering ideas

indicators.note: leaders come at the front, so this takes the first letters of English and Society

explanation.surface: A group of top figures in English high society propose thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Themes are subjects or topics, the main ideas of a work.

clue.text: Decay in small green vegetable or shrub

indicators.note: in says the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a pea is a small green vegetable

explanation.surface: Mould on a pea or on a bush in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The protea is a flowering South African shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The protea is a South African evergreen bush with large flower heads.

clue.text: Full relief after only 50 per cent relief brings freedom

indicators.note: after says the first piece follows the second
half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: ease is complete relief from pain or worry

explanation.surface: Total respite following partial respite finally liberates someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only 50 per cent' keeps the first half of the second relief; 'after' places the full relief behind that half.
explanation.definitionFit: A release is a liberation, as from prison or an obligation.

clue.text: Acclaim — Conservative meeting left-winger gets it

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the UK party
a red is a communist or socialist

explanation.surface: A Tory meets a socialist and finally understands.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is praise or recognition for an achievement.

clue.text: Badger-like creature surprisingly alert

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An animal resembling a badger is unusually watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is an African and Asian mammal related to weasels.

clue.text: Dance in a state of oblivion

definitions.meaning: a Caribbean dance passing under a lowered bar
a condition of being neglected or forgotten, in theology a place between heaven and hell

explanation.surface: Someone dances while unaware of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the bar-dance and an uncertain, forgotten condition.

clue.text: Soldiers having drinks with recreational drug get ill again

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of British soldiers
laps means drinks like a cat

explanation.surface: Troops drinking and taking ecstasy fall sick once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to deteriorate after an improvement in health.

clue.text: Having no weapons and lacking ability to punch, say?

definitions.meaning: punching needs arms, so a figure without limbs cannot do it

explanation.surface: Defenceless and unable to throw a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means weaponless and, playfully, literally armless.

clue.text: Boxer went to ground briefly

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: alit means landed, came down to the ground

explanation.surface: A fighter took cover for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went to ground' usually means hid; here it means landed.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was the heavyweight champion fighter.

clue.text: Too restricted by ceremonial sometimes

indicators.note: restricted by means held within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Rituals are occasionally excessively limited.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too both mean in addition or as well.

clue.text: Her good faith sorted out answer to alcohol problem?

indicators.note: sorted out implies the letters are put back into a different order

explanation.surface: A woman's sincere belief helps cure drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a morning drink taken to cure a hangover.
